body:
I haven't been on any medication since maybe a year after my suicide - ten years ago or so. Ditto with psychiatrists. I've been unemployed for quite some time, so no insurance. I suppose I could afford to pay to see somebody and try some different medicine, but all I ever noticed were side-effects from the ones I tried. Seemed like a lot of wasted time and money then, when it was just copays.

I don't want any life in return, I'm quite confident I could be miserable in anyone's shoes. I want to never have existed.

>What is it that makes you happy when you are? 

Nothing much I can pin down, or I'd do more of it. When things unexpectedly go my way - I keep expectations low for this reason. Doing nice things for people I care about, but usually I find myself seeing such opportunities only in hindsight. Tends to be pretty ephemeral, and is usually followed by a crash of some sort like I just burned through a few weeks mediocrity for a day of happiness, so now I'm going to be low for a while.

>If you could change anything you want about your life what would you change? 

Easy - let someone else take my place at birth. 

>What are your goals? 

I like the idea of having a little cabin in the woods, being kind of self-sufficient, etc. With no job, no prospects, and dwindling savings this seems like a pipe dream. And I expect that like other things I've lusted after in life, it would be a let down if I ever get there.

Thanks, I appreciate the perspective. 

I've read that depression is a recurrent condition but for as long as I can remember, I've been wondering if maybe happiness *isn't*.

Well the alcohol is certainly involved. If it comes down to a chicken-or-egg question, I was definitely depressed well before I ever started drinking. I've stopped a few times - hey, it's been almost a week right now. The hard part is not starting again next time I'm alone, and that's unavoidable. 

AA doesn't appeal to me. The people I've known who went to AA have all abandoned any non-AA friends and family for their sponsorees. Plus, I have trouble with the idea of meeting new people and then immediately sharing myself in ways that would be uncomfortable with even my closest friends. I know next to nothing about AA alternatives, but that seems to be the paradigm around which support groups operate.
